about.text: A soft, chalk-white Cypriot whey cheese, usually made from the whey left over from halloumi or kefalotyri with a little goat or sheep milk added. Eaten fresh with carob syrup or honey, or salted and dried hard for grating.

how.text: The whey is heated slowly to 65 °C, the milk goes in, and heating goes on under stirring. At 80–85 °C small crumbly curds appear. They are skimmed off with a slotted spoon, drained and cut in blocks. No starter and no rennet are used, only heat.

processing.text: Only the dried kind is matured: gently heated or sun-dried and matured until too hard to cut. No time given.
